top_choice_rationale: P001 (Melitz and Helpman, firm heterogeneity and selection) rests on an identifiable originating model (Melitz 2003) and a co-developed extension (Helpman-Melitz-Yeaple on exporting versus FDI). It is a different mechanism from the 2008 trade prize, which covered representative-firm new trade theory. Its central claim, that selection and reallocation across firms shape gains from trade, has been tested for over twenty years on firm-level customs and administrative data from many countries. Welfare magnitudes depend on functional form, but the qualitative result has held up. The main cost is that Bernard, Jensen, Eaton and Kortum are not credited on this entry, so the citation should name the theoretical framework and not all firm-level trade research. I rank P002 second because of its breadth of influence and its separable originators (Calvo, Taylor, Woodford). Its credit is more diffuse, though, and micro evidence on state-dependent pricing qualifies Calvo's mechanism. I rank P003 third because it is a clean two-author mechanism, but its collateral channel is less cleanly identified empirically and sits closer to the 2022 prize. I rank no award last because each of the three proposals is a mature, defensible achievement. I rank on achievement, maturity, attribution and citation scope, not on supporter counts.
